propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref in S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous SHAs and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable

git-remote-s3's built-in Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts that crash on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's events, causing data loss from an append-only event log

rebar's non-FF recovery already losslessly merges divergent git heads via iterated 2-parent merges and reuses merge=ours for derived files; the multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence at the bundle-storage layer, reducible to the solved git case

The heal must write the merged bundle before deleting any original, never delete the merged bundle, and hold the helper's per-ref lock throughout to guarantee at every crash point that >=1 bundle carrying full merged history remains remotely
Concurrent doctors must serialize via the helper's S3 lock (outer) and rebar's write_lock (inner), with backing-off processes converging on the winner's collapsed remote without self-healing

The doctor folds N divergent heads via iterated 2-parent merges (not octopus), following sync's existing lossless semantics, and applies --allow-unrelated-histories for heads sharing no common ancestor with HEAD
